lines.text: Drop a book on a desk, and it just sits there. Why? Everything that moves... or refuses to move... follows three simple rules by Isaac Newton.
Newton's first law is inertia. Look at the free body diagram. Gravity pulls down with m g, and the table pushes up with normal force.
Since both forces are equal and opposite, net force is zero, so acceleration is zero. An object stays at rest, or keeps moving steady, until an unbalanced force acts.
Now push the box. Newton's second law says force equals the rate of change of momentum. Momentum p is mass times velocity, so change in momentum is m times v minus u.
Divide by time t, and v minus u over t is just acceleration a. That gives us the famous formula... F equals m times a, measured in Newtons.
Here's the intuition. Push a light box and a heavy box with the exact same force. More mass means less acceleration.
Finally, Newton's third law. Every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Look closely at both free body diagrams.
When skater A pushes skater B, force A B equals minus force B A. They never cancel out, because they act on two different bodies.
Zero net force means no change. F equals m a tells us how fast things speed up. And forces always come in pairs. Physics, made simple.

scenes.brief: Hook: book drops and rests still on blueprint desk; kinetic type WHY DO THINGS MOVE? -> 3 LAWS OF MOTION
1st Law Inertia + FBD (mg down, F_N up, equal arrows) + ΣF = 0, a = 0, then unbalanced F_app pushes block
2nd Law unbalanced FBD (F_app > f, F_N = mg) + step-by-step Class 10 derivation p=mv -> F ∝ m(v-u)/t -> F=ma
2nd Law intuition: same force F=12N on 1kg vs 4kg blocks showing a = F/m with proportional acceleration vectors
3rd Law action-reaction push-off + two separate FBDs side by side (F_AB on A, F_BA on B), F_AB = -F_BA, two bodies never cancel
Recap lockup of all 3 formulas (ΣF=0, F=ma, F_AB=-F_BA) and closing beat PHYSICS, MADE SIMPLE.
